| [`position-area-scrolling-002.tentative.html`](https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/position-area-scrolling-002.tentative.html) | Fail | 5 / 6 | TEST BUG | "Reattach at 40,60" expects the boxes reattached in the same animation frame (`display: none`, a forced style update, then `display: block`) to keep the scroll offsets remembered before (the layout at 0,0, e1 at x=100), as its comment says ("there will be no anchor recalculation point" before the ResizeObserver events of an earlier draft); https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#anchor-recalculation-point now says that an anchor recalculation point occurs "whenever that element begins generating boxes (aka switches from display:none [...]) identical to when it starts running CSS animations", so the boxes are laid out with the remembered scroll offsets 40,60 (e1 at x=80); the subtest also expects `offsetLeft` right after `container.style.display = "flow-root"` (no recalculation point) not to include the default scroll shift that the previous subtest includes at the same scroll position (x=100 instead of 60), Chromium's snapshot of the scroll offsets taken once per frame; tentative, Firefox fails it with the result of the specification (e1 x = 80) |
| [`position-area-scrolling-003.tentative.html`](https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/position-area-scrolling-003.tentative.html) | Pass | 3 / 3 |  |  |

| [`scroll-to-anchored-fixed-004.html`](https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/scroll-to-anchored-fixed-004.html) | Fail | 0 / 1 | TEST BUG | the test expects the fixed box with `position-area: center span-all; left: calc(100vw - 5em)` not to follow its anchor in the horizontal axis (its reference resets the horizontal scroll position after the focus: the viewport must only scroll in the other axis), as Chrome and Safari do when the tracks of `position-area` are `span-all` in an axis; css-anchor-position-1 says that a box compensates for scroll "in the horizontal or vertical axis" when "abspos has a non-none value for position-area" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#compensate-for-scroll, no condition on the axis), so the library moves the box with the document in both axes and `focus()` (which now scrolls the viewport for an anchored fixed box) also scrolls the viewport in the horizontal axis; Firefox fails too |
